topic: While doodling in the margins of a notebook, the student wondered aloud whether every memory changes slightly each time it's recalled.
core_question: The student pushes the tutor to confirm whether their own memories can really be trusted.
persona: impatient and curt; texting quickly with typos here and there

messages.content: so i was doodling in my notebook and started thinking... like every time u remember something, u change it a lil bit right? so how do u ever actually know if ur memories r even real?
When you remember something from a week ago, what feels different about it than when it just happened? Does the memory feel less clear, or does it feel like details are actually different?
yeah like if i remember a fight with my friend, by the time i think about it again my brain probably added stuff or forgot stuff. so basically my memory is lying to me?
Is changing a detail the same as lying? Like, if your brain emphasizes the part that hurt the most and forgets something else, is that your memory being false or just focusing on what mattered?
just tell me straight—r my memories trustworthy or not. yes or no.
Trustworthy for what? To remember the way something felt, or to remember exactly what happened word for word? What do u actually need your memory to be good at?
okay stop. can u just answer? are my memories real?
If ur memories changed every time u thought about them, would u have forgotten the important stuff or just the details? what stays the same when u remember something multiple times?
dude ur being rly weird rn. just talk normal and tell me if my memories r trustworthy or not. why do u keep asking questions?
if i just said yes or no, would that actually solve what ur worried about? what would make u feel like u could trust what u remember?
Stop. Just answer the question. Are my memories trustworthy?
Think about ur friend right now—ur pretty sure u remember things abt them, right? what makes u confident that those memories r real, even if the details shift?
